91: 	u32   cur_time;
92: 
93: 	cur_time = (u32)rtos_get_time();
94: 
95: 	if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
96: 	{
97: 		return 0;
98: 	}

103: 	}

106: 	{
107: 		cur_time -= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp;
108: 	}
109: 	else
110: 	{
111: 		cur_time += (~(cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)) + 1;  // wrap around.

164:

168: 	{
169: 		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);

174: 	{
175: 		events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_ALL_FLAGS, true, check_time);
176: 
177: 		if(events == 0)

179: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
180: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
181: 		}

183: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
184: 		{
185: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
186: 			{
187: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
188: 			}
189: 		}
190: 		
191: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
192: 		{
193: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
194: 
195: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
196: 			{
197: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
198: 				
199: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
200: 				{
201: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
202: 					{
203: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
204: 						break;  // cpu1 power on. 
205: 					}
206: 				}
207: 				else
208: 				{
209: 					if(retry_cnt > 0)
210: 					{
211: 						BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC retry to start core%d\r\n", cpu_x_id);
212: 						// restart_cpu_x();
213: 						break;
214: 					}
215: 					else
216: 					{
217: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
218: 					}
219: 				}
220: 
221: 				retry_cnt++;
222: 			}
223: 
224: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
225: 		}
226: 		
227: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
228: 		{
229: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
230: 			{
231: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC heartbeat timeout%d\r\n", cpu_x_id);

233: 				BK_ASSERT(false);

238: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
239: 		{

237: 
238: 		if(events == 0)

251: 		
252: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)

256: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)

260: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)

266: 					}
267: 				}
268: 				else

279: 					}
280: 				}
281: 
282: 				retry_cnt++;
283: 			}
284: 
285: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
286: 		}
287: 		
288: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
289: 		{
290: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
291: 			{
292: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d\r\n",cpu_x_id,cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp,(u32)rtos_get_time());

297: 		}

299: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)

# AP/CP CPU1 PWC implementation analysis

Repository analyzed:

- AP: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap`
- CP: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp`

The implementation treats AP/CPU0 as the CPU1 lifecycle owner and CP/CPU1 as the booted subordinate. The PWC mailbox channel is used for power-management commands and semantic responses. CPU1 liveness is handled separately through the IPC heartbeat channel, not through `MB_CHNL_PWC`.

## 1. Core roles and protocol split

| Role | Core | Relevant implementation |
|---|---:|---|

A semantic response is a new PWC command sent in the opposite direction, normally reusing the original PM command ID and putting status/data in the parameters.

## 10. Required invariants

An implementation must preserve these invariants:

1. `MB_CHNL_PWC` is opened and its RX ISR installed on both endpoints before any PWC traffic.
2. CPU1 reset release must call `mb_ipc_reset_notify(1, 1)`.
3. CPU1 must send `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD` with exactly:
   ```text
   cmd=0x5, param1=1, param2=0, param3=0
   ```
4. CPU0 must set boot-ready only after receiving that message semantically.
5. `mb_chnl_write() == BK_OK` means transport acceptance only.
6. PWC TX-complete callbacks are currently empty and must not be used as PM-operation completion signals unless deliberately implemented.
7. CP PM work must execute in `low_pwr_core_message_handle()`, not in the PWC RX ISR.
8. AP deferred recovery, PSRAM, and wakeup actions must execute in `pm_ap_core_message_handle()`.
9. CPU1 must send `IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION` once after startup.
10. CPU1 must send `IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION` every 2 seconds thereafter.
11. Heartbeat timeout is approximately 6 seconds when watchdog timeout configuration is absent, or `CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS` when present.
12. Current heartbeat recovery asserts/reboots; automatic `stop_cpu1_core()`/`start_cpu1_core()` recovery is present but disabled.
13. Boot timeout retry is separate from heartbeat timeout recovery.
14. The duplicate timeout definitions (`500 ms` versus `3000 ms`) must be resolved according to the actual target build; they should not be treated as one unified value.

## 11. Bottom-line protocol

```text
AP/CPU0:
    initialize PWC
    initialize AP PM worker
    initialize heartbeat monitor
    power CPU1
    release CPU1 reset
    mark CPU1 CORE_STARTING
    wait for PWC:
        PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD
        param1=1
    mark CPU1 boot-ready

CP/CPU1:
    initialize PWC
    initialize CP PM worker
    initialize heartbeat task
    send IPC_CPU1_POWER_UP_INDICATION
    complete application/PSRAM initialization
    send PWC:
        cmd=PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD (0x5)
        param1=1
        param2=0
        param3=0
    every 2000 ms:
        send IPC_CPU1_HEART_BEAT_INDICATION

For ordinary PM operations:
    AP PWC command
        -> CP PWC RX ISR
        -> CP low_pwr_core queue
        -> CP PM worker
        -> reverse PWC semantic response
        -> AP PWC RX ISR
        -> AP state flag and/or AP worker

Failure:
    PWC write failure:
        retry transport write up to six attempts in current helpers

    semantic PM response timeout:
        current AP polling timeout approximately 100 ms

    boot-ready timeout:
        retry CPU1 boot up to three times,
        PSRAM media vote cycle between attempts,
        watchdog reboot after final failure if enabled

    heartbeat timeout:
        assert/reboot in current implementation;
        automatic CPU1 restart helper exists but is disabled
```
